extracted.intended_audience: economists considering submitting manuscripts to The Review of Economic Studies (authors) and readers interested in the journal's submission/review process
extracted.subtask_description: Information for authors about The Review of Economic Studies as a submission venue, emphasizing the journal's standing, editorial review aims, submission volumes, and turnaround statistics. Useful for deciding whether to submit and for setting expectations about review timing and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal standing / prestige
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review of Economic Studies is one of the core journals in economics. It is essential reading for economists, consistently ranking among the top five journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This positioning signals high selectivity and prestige; authors should factor the journal's top-tier status into expectations about difficulty of acceptance and audience reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial review aim: efficiency and high quality
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim to provide an efficient and high quality editorial review process to our authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the journal's stated goal for how submissions are handled. Authors can expect the editorial workflow to prioritize both speed and rigor, though actual timings are given by the turnaround statistics (see related metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission volume and refereeing proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: We now receive nearly 2,000 submissions per year, of which half go through a full refereeing procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies a substantial initial editorial screening/desk-rejection stage (approximately half of submissions do not proceed to full referee review). Authors should prepare submissions to pass initial editorial assessment (clarity of contribution, fit, presentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround statistics (review timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Turnaround statistics for submissions (July 2024 - June 2025): Decisions taken 1,555; Mean decision time on new submissions 55 days; Mean decision time on a first round submission that ends in resubmission decision 138 days; Decisions > 7 months (210 days) 0.6%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete performance metrics for the journal's speed of decision-making over the specified year. Authors can use these numbers to set expectations for time-to-decision for new submissions and for rounds that result in resubmission decisions; the very low share of decisions taking over 7 months indicates relatively fast processing overall.
